prompt: Implement the nexus vitals health gate per ADR-2026-06-04-1740. Five tasks, in priority order. (1) FIX THE BUSY-SPIN [DONE 2026-06-04 — jemalloc shipped, idle CPU 600%->0%, validated; remaining sub-item (b) typed-deserialize is lower priority]: nexus burned ~6 cores at idle via glibc malloc ARENA-LOCK CONTENTION. perf(symbol build)+perf trace proved it: self-CPU = serde_json::Value::clone/deserialize_any/drop + _int_malloc/_int_free + __lll_lock_wait_private; one worker did 331848 futex/4s (36% EAGAIN). Driver = every STDB adapter parses SQL into untyped serde_json::Value (sql_query()->Vec<Value>) + clones rows, called by ~20 short-interval polls (org_responder 4s, supervisor/integrator 5s, etc.) on SELECT * of growing tables (rl_q_entry, rl_pattern, agent, message, workplan_task); all funneled through 2 arenas because nexus.rs:417 sets MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 (ADR-2026-05-22-1720). PROVEN: restart with MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=16 => idle CPU 600%->0% (RSS 1.1GB). The arena cap is the wrong lever (trades CPU vs the 25GB RSS bloat it was added to fix). FIX (supersede ADR-2026-05-22-1720): (a) swap global allocator to jemalloc/mimalloc (per-thread caches, no global arena-lock storm) — fixes BOTH the RSS fragmentation AND the contention, then REMOVE MALLOC_ARENA_MAX; validate over a multi-hour run that RSS stays bounded AND idle CPU low. (b) reduce allocation rate: deserialize STDB rows into typed structs via serde derive (not Value+clone); widen/cache the 4-5s polls or move to STDB push-subscriptions instead of SELECT * polling. Add a regression test asserting idle nexus CPU < ceiling. INTERIM: live daemon currently running MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=16 (relieved, non-durable — nexus.rs:417 reverts to 2 on normal restart). (2) AUTO-CALIBRATE PROVIDERS [DONE operationally 2026-06-04 — only the automation remains]: root cause is config_sync.rs:248 preloads providers and preserves existing scores but registers new/uncalibrated ones at default 0.0 and NEVER triggers calibration; calibrate-all only fires on manual POST /api/inference/calibrate-all or `hex inference test`, so providers sit at q=0.00 forever. Running calibrate-all by hand fixed 3/4 instantly (qwen2.5-coder 0.85, Qwen3-32B 0.92, DeepSeek-R1 0.99; qwen3.6:35b-a3b was true-OOM and de-registered). FIX: after config_sync preload and on any provider registration, best-effort async-trigger calibrate-all for providers at the uncalibrated-default score; introduce a sentinel (e.g. -1.0) to distinguish 'never calibrated' from a real scored 0.0 so routing/health-gate can tell them apart. NOTE: the 'model=probe -> HTTP 404' startup log line is an UNRELATED health-check, not the calibration path — do not chase it. (3) AUTO-RELEASE GUARD: hex-cli/src/commands/nexus.rs find_nexus_binary() resolves [debug, release] — make the --daemon path prefer target/release (debug only via explicit HEX_NEXUS_BIN or a --dev flag) and warn loudly if a debug binary is ever resolved as a daemon. (4) HARD HEALTH GATE: add `hex doctor vitals` (also run at swarm-dispatch, surfaced by hex go / hex pulse) that HARD-FAILS on: nexus self-CPU over threshold while no inference is in flight, any provider q=0.00, STDB unreachable, or debug-build daemon. (5) PRODUCTIVITY WATCHDOG: nexus background task flags any swarm 'active' > N hours with zero commits AND zero completed tasks, auto-pauses it, and raises a priority-2 inbox notification. HARD CONSTRAINT: cargo build -p hex-nexus --release and cargo build -p hex-cli --release must exit 0; add tests for tasks 1, 3, 4, 5.
notes: Authored from the 2026-06-04 operator autopsy: 5-day debug daemon, zero swarm output, 3/4 providers q=0.00, silent ~4-core busy-spin. Task 2 (probe) is the bootstrap unblock — until local inference recovers, the planner/personas cannot reliably expand or execute this plan, so do task 2 first if running through the factory.
